help.title: Regression reliability limit analysis with censored and uncensored data
help.body:
Description
Regression Reliability Limit Analysis with Censored and Uncensored Data

Purpose
This analysis performs a regression-based statistical tolerance limit analysis to determine the maximum (or minimum) allowable value of a process input variable — such as crimp diameter — that ensures a response variable — such as burst pressure — meets a minimum quality or safety threshold with a specified level of statistical confidence. When a Censor variable is provided (if not provided, behind the scene, a pseudo censor variable is created with all set to 0 i.e. non-censored), the analysis uses survival censored regression model (survreg) using maximum likelihood estimation, which correctly handles measurements that were cut off by instrument limits — for example, burst pressures recorded as 25 psi when the true value was at least 25 but unknown.

Input data required to perform the analysis

Select your Response variable (e.g., Burst.Pressure) into the Response field and your Input variable (e.g., Crimp.Diameter) into the Input field
If your data includes censored observations, select the Censor variable into the Censored field — this variable should contain 1 for censored observations (where the true response value was not fully observed) and 0 for uncensored observations;
Leaving the censor field empty will treat all data as uncensored (i.e., create internaly a pseudo Censor variable with all set to 0)
Enter the Response Limit — the minimum acceptable response value for a lower limit analysis, or
Enter the maximum acceptable value for an upper limit analysis.
Set the Confidence Level (default 0.95)
Set Target Reliability (default 0.999) to define the statistical stringency of the tolerance limit
Select Lower Limit if the response must stay above the threshold (e.g., burst pressure must exceed a minimum), or
Upper Limit if the response must stay below the threshold.
Optionally check Additional plots for residuals to generate diagnostic plots, and
Check Flip axis for the P-P plot to display the P-P plot with axes transposed
